title: Derived tensor and Hom restriction comparisons compatible with evaluation
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and U any open. Choose derived categories [def-pc-derived-category] of module sheaves on X, every over-site of X, and U, in a common localization universe. Let R be exact over-site restriction followed by the canonical over-site equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]. Use the shared derived tensor [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure], derived internal Hom H and H_U [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], and canonical tensor-Hom families e_X and e_U [def-pc-canonical-derived-tensor-hom-bijection]. There exist simultaneous families t(K,L):R(K tensor L)≅R(K) tensor R(L) and h(L,E):R(H(L,E))≅H_U(R(L),R(E)), for all derived objects K,L,E, satisfying R(a tensor b);t(K′,L′).hom=t(K,L).hom;(R(a) tensor R(b)) for every a:K→K′ and b:L→L′, and t(K,L).hom;e_U(R(ξ);h(L,E).hom)=R(e_X(ξ)) for every ξ:K→H(L,E). There is no chosen tensor model, boundedness or quasi-coherence hypothesis.

source.place: Tags 079U, 08DL and 08DJ; evaluation after exact open restriction

proof.text: Obtain the bifunctorially natural tensor comparison by transporting the existing derived-pullback monoidal model through the natural isomorphism identifying open pullback with exact restriction.

Define m(L,E) explicitly by currying the composite of inverse tensor comparison with restriction of evaluation at identity of H(L,E). The evaluation-mate invertibility theorem gives IsIso m; let h=asIso m.

Uncurry R(xi);m by first-variable naturality of the canonical equivalence on U. Substitute the definition of m and cancel Equiv.apply_symm_apply. Use tensor naturality for (xi,identity L), cancel t.hom;t.inv, combine the functor maps of a composite, and use first-variable tensor-Hom naturality on X to get R(eX(xi)).

lean.statement:
theorem exists_derivedRestriction_tensorHom_coherence
    (X : Scheme.{uX}) (U : X.Opens)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wD} (SheafOfModules.{uX} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ V : X.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{wD} (SheafOfModules.{uX} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over V))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wD} (SheafOfModules.{uX} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))] :
    let R := ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{uX} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U) ⋙
      Equivalence.functor
        (C := SheafOfModules.{uX} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
        (D := SheafOfModules.{uX} (moduleRings U.toScheme.toRingedSpace))
        (Modules.overEquiv U)).mapDerivedCategory
    let H := derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology X.toRingedSpace)
      X.toRingedSpace.sheaf
    let HU := derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology U.toScheme.toRingedSpace)
      U.toScheme.toRingedSpace.sheaf
    ∃ (t : ∀ K L : schemeDerivedCategory X, R.obj (K ⊗ L) ≅ R.obj K ⊗ R.obj L)
      (h : ∀ L E, R.obj (H.obj (op L, E)) ≅ HU.obj (op (R.obj L), R.obj E)),
      (∀ K K' L L' (a : K ⟶ K') (b : L ⟶ L'),
        R.map (a ⊗ₘ b) ≫ (t K' L').hom =
          (t K L).hom ≫ (R.map a ⊗ₘ R.map b)) ∧
      (∀ K L E (ξ : K ⟶ H.obj (op L, E)),
        (t K L).hom ≫ schemeDerivedTensorHomEquiv U.toScheme
          (R.obj K) (R.obj L) (R.obj E) (R.map ξ ≫ (h L E).hom) =
        R.map (schemeDerivedTensorHomEquiv X K L E ξ))
